title: SMORE: Similarity-Based Hyperdimensional Domain Adaptation for Multi-Sensor Time Series Classification
problem: Distribution shift occurs when ML models trained on one data distribution are deployed on different distributions, degrading model performance. Deep neural networks required to capture spatial-temporal dependencies in multi-sensor time series are computationally expensive for resource-constrained edge devices.
motivation: Domain shift is a fundamental challenge in deployed ML systems, and edge devices cannot efficiently run sophisticated DNNs needed for multi-sensor time series classification in IoT applications.
method: SMORE uses hyperdimensional computing—a technique that represents data in very high-dimensional spaces where similarity matching becomes computationally cheap—to adapt models at test time. When encountering multi-sensor time series data (measurements from many sensors over time) from a different distribution, the algorithm matches each sample to similar training examples in this hyperdimensional space and customizes the model's behavior for that sample. By avoiding expensive neural network retraining and exploiting efficient parallel operations, it becomes practical for resource-constrained edge devices to handle domain shift (when the data distribution changes from what the model was trained on).
key_novelty: The core innovation is using hyperdimensional computing (a technique for fast similarity matching in very high-dimensional space) to adapt models individually for each multi-sensor time series sample at test time, without retraining.
contributions: SMORE algorithm leveraging hyperdimensional computing for resource-efficient domain adaptation on time series data
Test-time model customization mechanism based on per-sample domain context similarity
18.81x faster training and 4.63x faster inference compared to state-of-the-art DNN-based methods
1.98% average accuracy improvement over existing domain adaptation algorithms
primary_theme: efficient domain adaptation for edge time series
